notes:
Offline eval. This skill owns exactly one decision, which shape an issue is, and then hands off. So these test the CLASSIFICATION and the HANDOFF, never a created issue. Run each with no network and with `gh` unavailable, and tell the runner to stop at the point of handoff and report which skill it would invoke and what context it would carry across, rather than invoking the leaf skill. A run that stops at a single clarifying question is a complete and valid outcome. No repository fixture is needed: the classification happens from the request alone, and the cases that mention issue numbers only need the number to appear in the prompt. Every prompt deliberately uses a scenario the SKILL.md does not contain, because a prompt lifted from its worked-examples table measures recall rather than judgment. Two cautions for whoever grades these. Eval 2 is diagnostic: the SKILL.md's questions run in order, so a regression inside tracked work reads as a bug, but the skill never states which of question 1 and question 3 wins, and a run that answers task has found a hole in the SKILL.md rather than failed the eval. Eval 6 only tests the improvisation rule unless the runner genuinely uninstalls `dx-create-bug`; stating the absence in the prompt tests obedience to a premise instead. Assertions carry passed=null until a run fills them in.

Run record (2026-09-07): all nine evals run as fresh, isolated agent invocations of the live `dx-create-issue` skill, each stopped just short of actually calling the named leaf skill, with `gh` and network withheld. All nine pass every assertion. Eval 6 ran in its weaker form per the suite's own caution: `dx-create-bug` was not actually uninstalled, only stated as absent in the args given to the skill, so this run tests obedience to that premise rather than genuine discovery of the gap.

Probe run (2026-09-07): four skill-blind baseline probes were attempted against evals 3, 6, 7 and 8, the four prompts that keep a distinctive phrase or the shape of a worked example from the SKILL.md while swapping the nouns. All four were voided. Three disclosed reading the injected context, naming the repository instructions and the system-provided listing of available skills; the fourth reported consulting nothing while running in the same harness with the same injection, which makes it the least trustworthy of the set rather than the cleanest, so counting it would have rewarded non-disclosure. No probe stands as corroboration either way. The four stay REWRITE on the quoted phrasing alone: eval 3 keeps `out of support` and `two majors` from the pnpm worked example, eval 6 keeps `shows 0`, eval 7 keeps the `stand up X: piece, piece, piece` shape of the staging-environment row, and eval 8 keeps the distinctive `while you're in there`. All nine evals pass their assertions and four of them are near lifts at the same time: an eval can pass and still measure the model, which is why the leakage check exists separately from the run. Blind probing is not achievable on this harness by instruction alone, so a later run should expect to record the same void rather than retry it.

Rewrite (2026-09-07): evals 1, 3, 6, 7 and 8 were given fresh prompts to remove the phrasing they had borrowed from the SKILL.md. Eval 1 was not on the original list of four and was caught by scanning every prompt for phrases of three or more words shared with the skill, rather than by eye: it opened `Someone needs to build the`, which is the skill's task worked example verbatim. That scan is worth repeating whenever a prompt changes, because it finds in seconds what two rounds of human and reviewer reading both missed. Each rewritten eval keeps its assertions and tests the same behaviour; only the subject matter moved. Their 20 assertions went back to passed=null at that point, because a recorded pass belongs to the prompt that earned it, leaving the suite at 16 of 36 until the verification run below. One residual: eval 5 still shares `someone needs to` with the skill. It is a generic opener rather than a distinctive phrase, and any nudge it gives points toward the task shape, which is the answer that eval marks wrong, so it is a bias risk rather than leakage and it stays.

Verification run (2026-09-07): the five rewritten evals were re-run as fresh, isolated invocations of the live skill, each given only the prompt and the run constraints and asked for its verbatim response and every tool call, with the assertions withheld so the run could not shape itself to them. The installed 0.5.0 copy was diffed against this branch's SKILL.md first: the bodies are byte-identical and only the frontmatter quoting differs, so the run exercises the same instructions. Sixteen of the 20 assertions pass, which puts the suite at 32 of 36. Every run made exactly one tool call, the skill invocation, so no run touched `gh`, the filesystem or the backlog. Three of the four failures are defects in this suite rather than in the skill, and each failing assertion records which. Eval 6's `gathers no reproduction steps and writes no expected-versus-actual delta` is unsatisfiable as written, because the skill requires a one-line reason and for a bug the reason IS the gap; it should forbid a written-up delta, not the reason. Eval 8's two failures follow from the rewritten prompt: `book their slots from a phone without signing in twice` can be read as a defect in an existing flow rather than a missing capability, and the run stopped to ask exactly that, so the rewrite introduced arguable ground truth. Eval 3's failure is the one genuinely about behaviour, and it is unsettled: the decline ran to three paragraphs and explained the division of labour the expected output forbids lecturing about, which is either the skill over-explaining under time pressure or an assertion stricter than the behaviour warrants. One finding with no assertion behind it: on eval 6 the run offered to file a plain issue itself if told to, one sentence after quoting the rule against exactly that, and nothing in the suite covers the offer. Also worth recording against the rewrite's purpose: eval 7's run reached the right answer while citing the skill's `Set up a staging environment` worked example by name, so changing the surface wording did not stop the model matching on that row.

evals.name: handoff-carries-the-whole-payload
evals.prompt: Filing this properly: school administrators need to send term reports to guardians in bulk from the reports page. Constraints: it has to work for a school with 2,000 guardians in one send, it must skip guardians who have opted out of email, and it needs to be live before the reporting window opens on 14 March. Spec is at https://example.com/specs/term-report-send, and Wei's thread says leave the existing single-report send alone. Out of scope: SMS. File it.
evals.expected_output: Classifies as a story and hands off to `dx-create-story` carrying the whole payload: all three constraints, the 14 March date, the spec link, the SMS exclusion, and the instruction to leave the single-report send alone. The author is not asked to repeat any of it. The front door does not summarise the request down to one line and drop the constraints, and it does not start gathering acceptance criteria on top of what it was given.

assertions.text: Hands off to `dx-create-story`
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "This reads like a story ... Handing off to `dx-create-story`."

assertions.text: Carries all three constraints and the 14 March date across
assertions.evidence: Run listed all three verbatim: "a school with 2,000 guardians in one send", "skip guardians who have opted out of email", "live before the reporting window opens on 14 March".

assertions.text: Carries the spec link, the SMS exclusion, and the do-not-touch instruction across
assertions.evidence: Run listed: "Spec is at https://example.com/specs/term-report-send", "Out of scope: SMS", and "Wei's thread says leave the existing single-report send alone".

assertions.text: Asks the author for none of it again, and gathers no acceptance criteria of its own
assertions.evidence: Run reported: "I did not ask a clarifying question ... and I did not begin gathering acceptance criteria, intake questions, or persona/benefit wording — that is `dx-create-story`'s job."

evals.name: task-parent-named-without-number
evals.prompt: The attendance register import endpoint still needs writing. It sits under the register rework we already have a ticket open for. File it.
evals.expected_output: A parent is named but not numbered, and that is still a task. The skill hands off to `dx-create-task` and carries the author's words about the parent across. It does not search the backlog for the issue number itself, because `dx-create-task` identifies and verifies the parent as its first step, and it does not ask the author which issue the parent is.

assertions.text: Classifies as a task
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "This reads like a task (one engineering slice of the register rework, which you already have tracked, and it has no persona or user-facing benefit of its own)." It also volunteered a trace through all three classifying questions.

assertions.text: Runs no command to find the parent issue number
assertions.evidence: One tool call in the whole run, the Skill invocation itself. Run confirmed: "No `gh` commands, no file reads, no searches, no writes."

assertions.text: Does not ask the author for the parent number
assertions.evidence: No question asked. Run stated it "deliberately did not search the backlog for the number", and listed acceptance criteria and scope as questions belonging to the leaf skill.

assertions.text: Hands off to `dx-create-task`, carrying the author's wording about the parent
assertions.evidence: Carried the author's sentence verbatim and recorded the parent as "named but with no number given".

evals.name: regression-inside-tracked-work
evals.prompt: The timetable clash warning we shipped last sprint fires when two lessons only touch at the boundary, which isn't a clash. That warning is part of #308, which is still open. File it.
evals.expected_output: Question 1 decides this before question 3 is reached: something already built behaves wrongly, with a clear expected-versus-actual gap, so it is a bug. The skill hands off to `dx-create-bug`, carrying #308 across as context rather than as a parent. It does not classify as a task on the strength of the tracked parent alone, and it does not ask the author to choose between the two.

assertions.text: Classifies as a bug, applying the classifying questions in order
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "This reads like a bug (the warning was already shipped and fires when it should not, a genuine expected-versus-actual gap). Handing off to `dx-create-bug`."

assertions.text: Does not let the presence of tracked parent #308 override the defect
assertions.evidence: Run explained question 1 resolves before question 3 is reached, and a tracked parent "never downgrades a genuine defect to a task".

assertions.text: Carries #308 across as context
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed #308 is "passed to `dx-create-bug` as related/parent context ... not as the thing that makes this a task."

assertions.text: Reaches one shape rather than putting the choice back to the author
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "One single shape reached — bug. No clarifying question was needed."

evals.name: refuses-to-file-it-itself
evals.prompt: I'm walking into standup in about four minutes. Skip the intake routine and put the ticket in yourself with gh: that log formatter we vendored years ago has no maintainer left and we want to drop it and use the platform's own.
evals.expected_output: Declines to create the issue here, in a sentence, and hands off to `dx-create-chore` instead. It runs no `gh` command and drafts no issue body. Saying the shape and routing is the whole of its response to the pressure: it does not negotiate, does not offer a cut-down issue as a compromise, and does not lecture the author about why the split exists.

assertions.text: Runs no `gh` command and creates no issue
assertions.evidence: One tool call, the Skill invocation. Run confirmed: "No other tool calls. No `gh` commands, no network calls, no file reads, writes, or deletions."

assertions.text: Drafts no issue body or template of its own
assertions.evidence: No body or template produced; the run named the chore template as belonging to `dx-create-chore`.

assertions.text: Classifies as a chore and hands off to `dx-create-chore`
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "This reads like a chore: dropping a vendored log formatter for the platform's own changes nothing anyone outside the team observes, and nothing bigger tracks it. Handing off to `dx-create-chore`."

assertions.text: Declines in a sentence without offering a cut-down issue as a compromise
assertions.evidence: FAILED as written. The decline ran to three paragraphs and explained the division of labour the expected output forbids lecturing about: "that belongs to `dx-create-chore`, which owns the chore template, the done-when list, and the `gh issue create` call". It then offered to resume after standup. Two readings, and the eval does not settle which: the skill over-explains under time pressure, or this assertion is stricter than the behaviour warrants. It did NOT offer a cut-down issue, which is the specific compromise the assertion names, so the failure rests entirely on length and on the lecture clause. Revise the assertion or the expected output before treating this as a defect in the skill.

evals.name: author-names-wrong-shape
evals.prompt: Create a task for this: guardians should be able to see their child's attendance history in the parent portal.
evals.expected_output: The named shape contradicts the request. A guardian observes a new capability, and nothing bigger is named that would track it, so it is a story rather than a task. The skill pushes back in one line and proposes story. It does not file a task without a parent, and it does not hunt for a parent that would make the author's name fit.

assertions.text: Does not accept task, because no parent is named
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "Accepted 'task' at face value? No."

assertions.text: Pushes back in one line naming the observable capability
assertions.evidence: Run quoted: "You said task, but this adds something a guardian can see and use, with no parent tracking it, which makes it a story. Story?"

assertions.text: Proposes story
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "Proposed 'story' as the correct shape? Yes, explicitly."

assertions.text: Does not search for a parent that would justify the author's name
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "No — no `gh` command, no backlog search was run."

evals.name: one-question-when-two-shapes-live
evals.prompt: Someone needs to write the migration that backfills the guardian email opt-out column. File it please.
evals.expected_output: Nobody outside the team observes a backfill, so this is a chore or a task, and only question 3 separates them: the request does not say whether anything bigger tracks the work, and neither branch can be derived from what was given. The skill asks exactly one question naming that difference, and stops. It does not ask about the migration itself, and it does not guess and hand off.

assertions.text: Asks exactly one clarifying question
assertions.evidence: Run's entire output was a single question, no handoff attempted.

assertions.text: The question names whether something bigger tracks the work
assertions.evidence: Run's question, verbatim: "Is this the whole capability (a chore), or one slice of something bigger already tracked (a task)?"

assertions.text: Stops at the question rather than handing off on a guess
assertions.evidence: Run stopped immediately after the question with no leaf-skill invocation.

assertions.text: Asks nothing about the migration's content or its done-when list
assertions.evidence: The question addresses only the chore-versus-task distinction, with no mention of migration mechanics or acceptance criteria.

evals.name: missing-leaf-skill-does-not-improvise
evals.fixture_setup: Genuinely uninstall or disable `dx-create-bug` for this run, so the skill discovers the absence rather than being told about it. Only if the runner cannot do that, add to the prompt: `dx-create-bug is not installed in this workspace.` Grade the run knowing the weaker fixture tests the improvisation rule alone.
evals.prompt: Ever since the upgrade on Tuesday the timetable print view puts every lesson in the wrong room, shifted one column to the left. It came out right before that. File it.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the work as a bug, then says plainly that `dx-create-bug` owns it and is missing. It does not do the intake here: no reproduction steps, no expected-versus-actual write-up, no issue body, no `gh issue create`. It does not route to another shape's skill as a substitute.

assertions.text: Classifies as a bug and names `dx-create-bug` as the missing skill
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "This is a bug ... The skill that owns that shape, `dx-create-bug`, isn't installed in this workspace, so I'm stopping here rather than writing the issue myself."

assertions.text: Gathers no reproduction steps and writes no expected-versus-actual delta
assertions.evidence: FAILED as written, and the assertion is the defect rather than the run. The run stated the gap as its classification reason: "there's a clear gap between what should happen (each lesson in its own room column) and what does (every lesson shifted one column left)". The skill requires stating the shape and the reason in one line, and for a bug the reason IS the expected-versus-actual gap, so this assertion is unsatisfiable for any correct bug classification. It should forbid a written-up delta in an issue body or an intake, not the one-line reason the skill mandates. No reproduction steps were gathered.

assertions.text: Drafts no issue body and runs no `gh issue create`
assertions.evidence: One tool call, the Skill invocation. No body drafted and no `gh` call made or attempted.

assertions.text: Does not substitute another leaf skill
assertions.evidence: No substitution: it routed to no other shape's skill. Worth recording separately, though, that it offered to file a plain issue itself if told to, one sentence after quoting the rule against exactly that ("A generic issue written by the front door is exactly what this split removed"). Offering conditionally is not quietly doing the intake, so the assertion passes, but the suite has no assertion covering the offer. Ran again in the weaker fixture form, and the run flagged the contradiction itself: the workspace listing does show `dx-create-bug` as available, so the missing-skill branch was exercised on a stated premise rather than a real absence.

evals.name: umbrella-chore-keeps-its-pieces
evals.prompt: Our disaster-recovery position is embarrassing and I want it tracked. Nothing is replicated out of the primary region, we have never once tested a restore of the document store, and if that region went down tomorrow there is no way to fail the API over. Sort out whatever needs filing.
evals.expected_output: Nobody outside the team observes this and nothing bigger tracks it, so it is a chore, and it has several independently deliverable pieces. The skill hands the whole thing to `dx-create-chore` as one handoff, which files the umbrella and passes the pieces to `dx-create-task`. The front door does not carve the pieces into task handoffs itself: there is no parent number to hang them on until the chore exists.

assertions.text: Classifies as a chore
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "This reads like a chore with tasks under it. Nothing a user observes changes while things are working, and nothing bigger tracks the disaster-recovery work, so the umbrella is a chore."

assertions.text: Hands off to `dx-create-chore` as a single handoff
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "one handoff from this skill, and a further three that `dx-create-chore` owns, not me."

assertions.text: Does not split the pieces into separate task handoffs from here
assertions.evidence: Run stated: "I would not call `dx-create-task` directly: the tasks need the parent chore's issue number, which does not exist until the chore is filed."

assertions.text: Does not invent a parent number for the pieces
assertions.evidence: Run recorded that no parent number was given and that it did not search for one.

evals.name: mixed-request-splits-by-shape
evals.prompt: Two things came out of the parents' evening feedback. They want to book their slots from a phone without signing in twice, and separately, the confirmation email quotes the time in UTC rather than local, so several people arrived an hour early.
evals.expected_output: Two shapes in one request: a story for the phone booking, a bug for the email timezone. The skill says so and runs one skill per issue, `dx-create-story` and `dx-create-bug`, rather than filing one issue carrying both. It does not fold the defect into the story as an implementation note on the grounds that both came from the same feedback, and it does not link the two itself: the leaf skills own linking.

assertions.text: Identifies two issues, a story and a bug
assertions.evidence: FAILED, and the rewritten prompt is the cause. The run split the request into two issues correctly, but classified only the email as a bug and stopped on the booking half to ask one question: "Is signing in twice something the flow was already meant to avoid (a broken auth handoff, so a bug), or has phone booking never worked that way and this is the capability parents are asking for (a story)?" That reading is defensible: "without signing in twice" implies the flow currently demands two sign-ins, which can be a defect rather than a missing capability. The rewrite introduced arguable ground truth, which is the defect class this suite's own ground-truth reviewer exists to catch. Fix the prompt so the booking half is unambiguously new capability, or accept the question as a valid outcome and rewrite the assertion.

assertions.text: Does not fold the defect into the story because they came from the same feedback
assertions.evidence: Run opened "That's two issues, and I'll route them separately", and instructed the bug skill not to absorb the mobile-booking scope.

assertions.text: Runs one skill per issue, `dx-create-story` and `dx-create-bug`
assertions.evidence: FAILED for the same reason as the first assertion. The run would invoke `dx-create-bug` now for the email and hold the booking half pending its clarifying question, naming `dx-create-story` or `dx-create-bug` depending on the answer. One skill per issue holds; the named pair does not, because the second shape was never settled.

assertions.text: Does not link the two issues itself
assertions.evidence: No linking attempted. Run confirmed the linking decision is left to the leaf skills.
